title: Enterprise intake rubric for polyglot client onboarding and streaming handshake ergonomics
creator: Aisha Patel
summary: Create a lightweight, actionable intake and prioritization rubric for enterprise customer requests related to client libraries (polyglot language support), authentication patterns (token rotation/KMS), and streaming ergonomics (handshake, backpressure, reconnect semantics). Deliver a decision framework to convert requests into scopes, default implementations, and engineering tickets.
background: Over the last 12 months we've seen a growing set of enterprise asks that combine three dimensions: language idiomatic client wrappers (Go, Java, .NET), secure auth integrations (KMS-backed key rotation, delegated OIDC token flows), and streaming ergonomics (initial handshake semantics, client-side backpressure, graceful reconnects). Current intake is ad-hoc and results in repeated design churn across SDK owners and duplicated engineering work. PM teams need a repeatable rubric to fast-track high-value requests into the backlog and to provide deterministic answers to customers.
goals: Define acceptance criteria for enterprise client feature requests so engineers have clear deliverables
Prioritize requests by measurable impact (security, latency, adoption) instead of subjective urgency
Provide canonical patterns (auth adapter, streaming handshake) that SDKs can adopt to reduce duplication
Reduce triage lead time from intake to scoped ticket from ~2 weeks to <72 hours for enterprise-tier customers
scope_in: Guidelines and decision tree for evaluating polyglot client requests
Standardized auth adapter interface and recommended token refresh patterns
Baseline streaming handshake spec (connect, auth exchange, resume token, backpressure signals, reconnect behavior)
Mapping rubric outcomes to release tracks (hosted quick-fix, dedicated SDK change, or enterprise-only integration)
Sample RFC templates and a gating checklist for security and compliance
scope_out: Full implementation of language bindings (this ticket outputs RFCs and prioritized set but not code delivery)
Backend server-side runtime changes beyond documented compatibility notes
Onboarding playbooks for customer success once feature is implemented (handled by ENABLE team)
proposed_solution: Build a 2-page intake rubric plus decision tree doc in Confluence and a 1-page summary for CSMs. The rubric will score requests across: security sensitivity, user count impact, code duplication avoided, latency/throughput impact, and implementation complexity. For streaming ergonomics: propose a minimal v1 handshake that includes: client-provided client_id, optional resume_token, server capability flags, and explicit backpressure window messages. For auth patterns: define a pluggable 'AuthAdapter' interface with methods for fetch_token(), refresh_if_needed(), and sign_request(), and provide reference pseudo-code in Go/Python/JavaScript. Deliverables: Confluence RFC, triage playbook, prioritized backlog CSV, and two seed engineering tickets for ENG-4812 and ENG-5120.
tradeoffs_and_risks: A lightweight handshake may not cover all advanced enterprise needs (e.g., per-tenant routing) — mitigate by versioning the handshake and allowing opt-in extensions
Providing sample AuthAdapter implementations increases maintenance surface; mitigate by keeping reference clients minimal and clearly labeled as "reference" rather than supported SDKs
Scoring rubric subjectivity — mitigate with calibrations: run rubric on last 30 intake items and iterate based on stakeholder feedback
acceptance_criteria: Confluence RFC published: 'Enterprise Client Intake Rubric v1' with decision tree and scoring matrix
One-page triage playbook for CSMs and Solutions with example scored requests
Canonical handshake spec and AuthAdapter interface posted in design repo with pseudo-code in Go/Python/TS
At least two engineering tickets created and linked: ENG-4812 (streaming handshake reference) and ENG-5120 (AuthAdapter reference impl)
Triage pilot executed on next 8 enterprise requests and measured: average triage time reduced to <72 hours
